title: code-review-mcp-server tool arguments permit shell command injection
summary: Caller-controlled folderPath and baseBranch values enter shell command strings in code review MCP tools. Crafted arguments can execute commands with the MCP server process permissions.

severity.rationale: Code execution requires control of tool arguments reaching the configured MCP server. Agent-generated arguments can meet this prerequisite in coding workflows, warranting a 72-hour response.

exposure: Applies to calls to getLocalGitDiff, codeReview, createPR and getPRTemplate using attacker-influenced folderPath or baseBranch values.

remediation.details: Use code-review-mcp-server 1.5.3 or later, which passes argument arrays to execFileSync instead of shell command strings. The vendor lists no workaround.
remediation.risk: Updating can interrupt dependent workflows; test compatibility before resuming them.

verification: Confirm the MCP process uses 1.5.3 or later; test normal diff and review tools.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
